domain_label: Frozen Pre-Registered Success Metric & Stopping Rule
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is the metric-and-stopping-rule design itself; the optimization engine that proposes candidates is delegated to sibling KBs
an eval loop exists that repeatedly scores candidate outputs against the metric and can be halted by a stopping rule
the team can compute a naive baseline, a human-curated baseline, and the metric's standard error before freezing
exclusions: the candidate-generation / optimization algorithm itself (delegated to the generation engine KBs)
causal-inference design of randomized experiments beyond OEC and guardrail definition
long-term post-deployment monitoring after the loop terminates
automated learning of the construct from data without human naming

competency_questions.question: How is an informal 'the results are good' turned into a single named, validated construct?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUCCESS_CONSTRUCT names the construct and CONSTRUCT_VALIDITY evidences it

competency_questions.question: Which observable indicators are chosen to reflect the construct and on what stance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDICATOR_SELECTION chooses indicators with a reflective/formative stance tied to the construct

competency_questions.question: How is it tested whether a proxy indicator actually tracks real downstream value?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROXY_VALIDITY estimates the proxy-to-true-value correlation and its breakdown conditions

competency_questions.question: How is the measure operationalized into one reproducible number?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MEASURE_OPERATIONALIZATION pins the estimator, population, window and computation

competency_questions.question: How are several proxies combined into one overall evaluation criterion?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OEC defines a single weighted decision metric over the proxies

competency_questions.question: What baselines must a result beat to count as good?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BASELINE_TO_BEAT fixes a naive and a human-curated baseline on the same population

competency_questions.question: How is the metric frozen and pre-registered so it cannot be redefined post-hoc?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FROZEN_METRIC locks measure+baseline+threshold into an immutable record before optimization

competency_questions.question: What hashed pre-registration artifact records the whole pre-commitment, and how is each frozen choice made explainable and tamper-evident?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREREGISTRATION_RECORD bundles and hashes the frozen elements and METRIC_PROVENANCE records the rationale behind each choice

competency_questions.question: What minimum per-cycle improvement counts as progress, and is it robust?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IMPROVEMENT_CRITERION requires delta_M>=epsilon and SENSITIVITY_ANALYSIS checks robustness

competency_questions.question: How is the loop kept from gaming the metric away from the construct?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOODHART guards metric-construct decoupling alongside the frozen metric

competency_questions.question: What secondary metrics must not regress while optimizing, and how is false discovery bounded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GUARDRAIL_METRICS bounds harm; MULTIPLE_COMPARISONS controls FDR across slices

competency_questions.question: What is the terminating stopping rule, how is each cycle's stop/continue/amend decided, and how is termination certified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STOPPING_RULE stops at threshold OR max_cycles, DECISION_GATE renders the verdict, and TERMINATION_CERTIFICATE certifies which arm fired

competency_questions.question: How is the max_cycles fuel budget accounted so the termination guarantee is enforced?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FUEL_BUDGET enforces max_cycles as a hard non-renewable ledger feeding the stopping rule

competency_questions.question: How is a frozen metric protected from silent drift and arbitrary specification?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: METRIC_DRIFT_AUDIT detects pipeline drift; SENSITIVITY_ANALYSIS tests specification robustness

glossary.definition: the unobservable quality 'good' is claimed to be, named and defined apart from any one number
an observable signal hypothesized to reflect the construct
the exact reproducible function (estimator + population + window) that yields the metric number M
overall evaluation criterion: one combined decision metric over the proxies (Kohavi)
a fixed anchor (naive/random and human-curated) the metric must exceed for a result to count
a pre-registered, immutable measure+baseline+threshold that cannot be redefined post-hoc
the minimum delta_M over baseline that counts as a genuine per-cycle improvement
the rule that halts the loop at threshold OR max_cycles, guaranteeing termination
when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure (Goodhart 1975; Strathern 1997)
false discovery rate: expected fraction of declared wins that are false, controlled by Benjamini-Hochberg
the fuel budget: the hard cap on optimization cycles whose exhaustion forces a stop
a secondary metric that must not regress while the OEC is optimized (Kohavi)

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for frozen pre-registered success-metric and stopping-rule work units, grounded in construct validity, online controlled experimentation, multiple-comparison control, and preregistration practice; no supplied dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Goodhart 1975 (Goodhart's law) and Strathern 1997 'Improving ratings: audit in the British University system'; Benjamini & Hochberg 1995 'Controlling the False Discovery Rate' (JRSS-B); Kohavi, Tang & Xu 2020 'Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments' (OEC, guardrail metrics); Cronbach & Meehl 1955 'Construct Validity in Psychological Tests' (Psychological Bulletin); Nosek et al. 2018 'The preregistration revolution' (PNAS)

nodes.definition: Turn the informal claim 'the results are good' into a single named latent construct (the unobservable quality being claimed, e.g. 'audience resonance' or 'editorial quality'), stated as a theoretical concept distinct from any one number that will later index it.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the underlying notion of what 'good' means for this asset changes

pros.claim: A named construct gives the whole loop a fixed referent so later disputes are about measurement, not about what 'good' even meant
pros.example: 'good thumbnail' is named as the construct click-through-worthiness, separable from any single CTR number

cons.claim: Naming a construct prematurely can reify a vague intuition into a target the team then over-trusts
cons.example: labelling 'engagement' as the construct hides that watch-time and shares pull in opposite directions

failure_modes: the construct is conflated with one convenient metric from the start
two stakeholders silently hold different constructs under the same word
acceptance_tests: the construct has a one-sentence definition and an explicit not-this list, agreed by >=2 stakeholders
revisit_triggers: the business definition of success for this asset is revised
a new stakeholder disputes what good means

nodes.definition: Establish construct validity in the Cronbach-Meehl sense: assemble the nomological net (the lawful relations the construct should have with other variables) and gather convergent and discriminant evidence that the named construct actually exists and is internally coherent before it is allowed to drive a loop.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: convergent/discriminant evidence shifts or the nomological net is revised

pros.claim: Construct validity makes 'we measured the right thing' an argued claim with evidence rather than an assertion
pros.example: share-rate and a human resonance rubric correlating r~0.6 is convergent evidence the construct is real

cons.claim: Full construct-validation is slow and can stall a loop that needs to start with an imperfect proxy
cons.example: demanding a validated nomological net before any iteration freezes a fast content pipeline

failure_modes: no discriminant evidence, so the construct is indistinguishable from a confound
the nomological net is assumed, never tested
acceptance_tests: at least one convergent and one discriminant relation are documented with their observed direction
revisit_triggers: a predicted relation in the nomological net is violated by data
the construct is reused in a new domain

nodes.definition: Select the observable indicator(s) that stand in for the latent construct: the measurable signals (e.g. share-rate, dwell-time, completion) hypothesized to reflect the construct, with an explicit reflective-vs-formative stance on how indicators relate to it.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a candidate indicator is added, dropped, or re-weighted

pros.claim: Explicit indicator selection separates 'what we observe' from 'what we mean', so a weak indicator can be swapped without redefining success
pros.example: completion-rate chosen as the indicator for 'narrative grip', leaving the construct intact if completion is later dropped

cons.claim: A single convenient indicator invites tunnel vision and tighter Goodhart pressure
cons.example: using only watch-time as the indicator for quality rewards padding

failure_modes: the indicator is chosen for availability, not for reflecting the construct
reflective and formative indicators are mixed without saying which is which
acceptance_tests: each indicator has a stated hypothesis linking it to the construct and a reflective/formative tag
revisit_triggers: an indicator's correlation with the construct degrades
a cheaper indicator becomes available

nodes.definition: Test proxy validity: quantify how well the chosen indicator (e.g. share-rate) actually tracks the real downstream value the construct is meant to capture, estimating the proxy-to-true-value correlation and the conditions under which it breaks down.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the proxy-to-true-value relationship is re-estimated or found unstable

pros.claim: Knowing the proxy's true-value correlation lets you weight or discount it instead of trusting it blindly
pros.example: share-rate correlates r~0.4 with renewal revenue, so it is treated as a noisy directional proxy not a target

cons.claim: Proxy-validity estimates are themselves uncertain and can lend false confidence to a weak proxy
cons.example: a one-off r~0.7 on a small sample is read as proof the proxy is value-aligned

failure_modes: the proxy is assumed valid because it is convenient
validity is estimated once and never re-checked as the distribution shifts
acceptance_tests: the proxy-to-true-value correlation is estimated with a confidence interval and stated breakdown conditions
revisit_triggers: the proxy decouples from downstream value in a holdout
the population the proxy was validated on changes

nodes.definition: Operationalize the measure M: pin the exact estimator, population, unit of analysis, aggregation window, and computation that turns indicators into a single number, so 'the metric' is a reproducible function, not a description.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the estimator, population, or aggregation window definition changes

pros.claim: A fully operational measure makes the number reproducible and auditable by anyone with the data
pros.example: M = mean(shares/impressions) over 7 days on logged-in users, ties broken by impression count

cons.claim: Over-specifying the estimator early can hard-code a choice (window, population) that later proves wrong and is costly to unwind once frozen
cons.example: freezing a 7-day window before learning the signal matures at 14 days

failure_modes: the metric is described in prose but never pinned to a single reproducible computation
population or unit of analysis is left ambiguous so two teams compute different numbers
acceptance_tests: two independent implementations of the estimator produce the same number on the same data
revisit_triggers: the estimator is found ambiguous in implementation
the data schema feeding the measure changes

nodes.definition: Define the Overall Evaluation Criterion (Kohavi): a single decision metric that combines the chosen proxies (and trade-offs between them) into one number the loop optimizes, so the team is not left arbitrating between several metrics every cycle.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the OEC weighting or its component proxies change

pros.claim: One OEC turns multi-metric debates into a single optimizable, pre-agreed objective the loop can act on
pros.example: OEC = 0.7*normalized_share_rate + 0.3*normalized_completion, agreed before iteration begins

cons.claim: Collapsing several proxies into one OEC hides trade-offs and can be gamed by pushing the cheapest component
cons.example: an OEC dominated by clicks rewards clickbait that tanks completion

failure_modes: the OEC is a post-hoc average chosen to make current results look good
component directions conflict so improving the OEC can worsen real value
acceptance_tests: the OEC is a single function of named components with fixed weights agreed before any optimization cycle
revisit_triggers: a component proxy is revalued or dropped
the OEC is found gameable by a degenerate strategy

nodes.definition: Establish the baseline(s) to beat: at minimum a naive/random baseline (what the metric scores with no skill) and a human-curated baseline (a strong reference the loop must exceed), so 'improvement' is defined against a fixed anchor rather than against the previous noisy cycle.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the baseline population, reference set, or computation changes

pros.claim: A fixed naive+human baseline turns the metric into a yardstick: a score is now meaningful relative to chance and to a strong human
pros.example: a share-rate of 0.04 means little until you know random is 0.01 and a human editor hits 0.05

cons.claim: A baseline computed on a non-comparable population silently inflates or deflates measured improvement
cons.example: a human baseline drawn from a premium audience makes the model look worse than it is

failure_modes: only the previous cycle is used as the reference, so noise reads as improvement
the baseline is recomputed each cycle, removing the fixed anchor
acceptance_tests: both a naive and a human-curated baseline are computed on the same population and unit as the live metric
the baseline values are frozen alongside the metric, not recomputed per cycle
revisit_triggers: the comparison population shifts away from the baseline population
a stronger human reference becomes available

nodes.definition: Pre-register and freeze the metric: lock the operational measure M, its baseline, and a success threshold into an immutable record (Nosek-style preregistration) before optimization begins, forbidding post-hoc redefinition of the metric to fit results.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the frozen metric, baseline, or threshold is proposed for amendment

pros.claim: Freezing the metric before results removes the degree of freedom that lets a team redraw the target around whatever happened
pros.example: the threshold M>=0.05 is registered and hashed before cycle 1, so a later 0.045 cannot be relabelled a success

cons.claim: A frozen metric that turns out mis-specified cannot be quietly fixed; amendment requires a visible, costly change-control step
cons.example: discovering the window was wrong forces a logged amendment that resets the comparison

failure_modes: the metric is 'frozen' but quietly amended when results disappoint (HARKing / outcome switching)
no immutable record exists, so the pre-registration claim is unfalsifiable
acceptance_tests: the metric, baseline and threshold are stored in an immutable, timestamped, owner-attributed record before any optimization cycle
any change to the frozen record is recorded as a dated amendment, never a silent edit
revisit_triggers: a mis-specification in the frozen metric is discovered
a stakeholder requests a metric change mid-loop

nodes.definition: Define the improvement criterion: require delta_M >= epsilon (a pre-set minimum effect size) over the frozen baseline for a cycle to count as progress, so trivial or noise-sized gains do not justify continuing the loop.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: epsilon, the effect-size definition, or the noise model changes

pros.claim: A minimum delta epsilon makes 'did this cycle improve things' a hypothesis test, not a glance at a noisy number
pros.example: require delta_M >= 0.5 sigma over baseline before a cycle is logged as an improvement

cons.claim: Setting epsilon too high discards real small gains; too low lets noise masquerade as progress
cons.example: epsilon below the metric's standard error declares random walk steps as wins

failure_modes: epsilon is smaller than the metric's noise, so the loop 'improves' on noise
delta is measured against the previous cycle rather than the frozen baseline
acceptance_tests: epsilon exceeds the metric's estimated standard error and is fixed before iteration
a cycle counts as progress only when delta_M over the frozen baseline meets epsilon
revisit_triggers: the metric's measured noise rises above epsilon
the effect-size convention for the domain changes

nodes.definition: Guard against Goodhart's law (Goodhart 1975; Strathern 1997 'when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure'): detect and prevent the optimization from gaming the frozen metric in ways that decouple it from the construct it was meant to index.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new gaming strategy is observed or the metric-construct gap widens

pros.claim: Explicit Goodhart guards catch the failure where the metric keeps rising while the real construct falls
pros.example: share-rate climbs while a human resonance audit drops, flagging the metric has become a gamed target

cons.claim: Aggressive anti-gaming checks can suppress genuine improvements that merely look like gaming
cons.example: penalizing every CTR jump as clickbait discourages legitimately better thumbnails

failure_modes: the metric is optimized to the point it no longer reflects the construct
gaming is only noticed after the construct has visibly degraded
acceptance_tests: a held-out construct check (e.g. human rubric) runs alongside the metric and a divergence triggers review
revisit_triggers: the metric and a construct audit diverge
a degenerate strategy that inflates the metric is discovered

nodes.definition: Define guardrail metrics (Kohavi): secondary metrics that must not regress while the OEC is optimized, so the loop cannot trade away safety, retention, or quality to win on the primary metric.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a guardrail metric or its non-regression bound changes

pros.claim: Guardrails let you optimize aggressively on the OEC while bounding collateral damage on what you are unwilling to lose
pros.example: allow share-rate gains only if unsubscribe-rate and complaint-rate stay within their bounds

cons.claim: Too many guardrails make every cycle fail some bound and stall the loop in over-caution
cons.example: a dozen guardrails each with tight bounds means no candidate ever clears them all

failure_modes: a guardrail metric is harmed silently because nobody is watching it
guardrails are added post-hoc to explain away an unwanted result
acceptance_tests: each guardrail has a pre-set non-regression bound checked every cycle alongside the OEC
revisit_triggers: a guardrail breach occurs
a new harm dimension emerges that no guardrail covers

nodes.definition: Control multiple comparisons: when the metric is evaluated across many fields, niches, segments, or cycles, apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control so the rate of false 'wins' is bounded and the loop does not declare success on noise found by searching many slices.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the number of comparisons or the target FDR level changes

pros.claim: FDR control bounds the expected fraction of false wins when scanning many niches, replacing naive per-test p-values
pros.example: testing 50 niches at q=0.1 via Benjamini-Hochberg keeps expected false discoveries near 10% of declared wins

cons.claim: FDR control reduces power, so real but small effects in some niches may be missed
cons.example: a genuine lift in one rare niche fails the adjusted threshold and is discarded

failure_modes: per-niche p-values are read without any multiplicity adjustment
the comparison family is defined after seeing which slices won (garden of forking paths)
acceptance_tests: the family of comparisons is declared before testing and Benjamini-Hochberg controls FDR at a pre-set level
revisit_triggers: the number of slices tested grows
the target FDR level is renegotiated

nodes.definition: Define the terminating stopping rule: stop the optimization loop when the frozen metric crosses its threshold OR when the max_cycles fuel budget is exhausted, whichever comes first. This conjunction of a frozen metric + baseline + threshold + max_cycles is exactly what makes the eval loop terminate (scope: R2 non-termination).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the threshold, max_cycles budget, or the stop condition logic changes

pros.claim: A threshold-OR-max_cycles rule guarantees the loop halts: either it wins or it runs out of fuel, never spins forever
pros.example: stop when M>=0.05 or after 8 cycles, so the loop provably terminates in at most 8 cycles

cons.claim: A max_cycles budget set too low stops a loop that was still genuinely improving toward the threshold
cons.example: halting at 8 cycles when the trajectory would have crossed the threshold at cycle 9

failure_modes: only a threshold stop exists, so a loop that never reaches it runs forever (R2 non-termination)
max_cycles is mutable mid-loop, defeating the termination guarantee
acceptance_tests: the loop halts deterministically when M crosses the frozen threshold or max_cycles is reached, whichever first
max_cycles is fixed in the frozen record so termination is bounded a priori
revisit_triggers: the fuel budget is repeatedly exhausted without crossing threshold
the threshold is found unreachable in principle

nodes.definition: Account the fuel budget: track and enforce max_cycles (and any per-cycle compute/cost ceiling) as a hard, non-renewable resource, so the stopping rule's max_cycles arm has a real ledger and the loop cannot quietly extend itself.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the max_cycles budget or per-cycle cost ceiling is changed

pros.claim: A hard fuel ledger makes the max_cycles arm enforceable: remaining budget is a tracked number, not a vibe
pros.example: a counter decrements each cycle and the loop refuses to start cycle 9 when budget is 8

cons.claim: A rigid fuel ledger with no contingency can waste a near-win that needed one more cheap cycle
cons.example: the loop halts with budget zero one cycle short of a clear threshold crossing

failure_modes: the budget is treated as advisory and silently extended when results look promising
no remaining-fuel counter exists, so max_cycles is never actually enforced
acceptance_tests: a monotone non-renewable counter enforces max_cycles and blocks any cycle beyond the frozen budget
revisit_triggers: the budget is exhausted without a decision
compute cost per cycle changes materially

nodes.definition: Audit for metric drift: detect when the data pipeline, population, or computation feeding a frozen metric silently changes so that the 'same' frozen metric no longer measures the same thing, which would invalidate the comparison to the frozen baseline.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the pipeline, schema, or population feeding the frozen metric changes

pros.claim: Drift auditing protects the integrity of a frozen comparison by catching when 'the metric' silently mutated
pros.example: a logging change halves impression counts, detected before it is mistaken for a metric drop

cons.claim: Over-sensitive drift alarms create noise that erodes trust in the freeze
cons.example: every minor schema tweak fires a drift alert and the team starts ignoring them

failure_modes: a pipeline change shifts the metric and is read as a real movement
the frozen computation is altered without a recorded amendment
acceptance_tests: the frozen metric's input distribution and computation hash are monitored and any change raises a drift flag
revisit_triggers: an input distribution shift is detected
the metric computation hash changes unexpectedly

nodes.definition: Run sensitivity analysis: vary the metric's free choices (window, weights, population, epsilon) and confirm the stop/continue decision is robust, so the conclusion does not hinge on one arbitrary frozen choice.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a free analysis choice is found to flip the decision

pros.claim: Sensitivity analysis shows whether a win survives reasonable alternative choices or is an artifact of one window
pros.example: the threshold crossing holds across 7/14/28-day windows, so it is not a windowing artifact

cons.claim: A wide sensitivity sweep can manufacture a specification where any result looks fragile
cons.example: testing 40 weighting schemes is sure to find one where the decision flips

failure_modes: the decision rests on a single arbitrary specification never stress-tested
sensitivity is run only over choices that confirm the desired answer
acceptance_tests: the stop/continue decision is shown stable across a pre-declared set of reasonable alternative specifications
revisit_triggers: a reasonable alternative specification flips the decision
a previously fixed choice becomes contested

nodes.definition: Produce the preregistration record: a single immutable, timestamped artifact (Nosek-style) bundling the construct, indicators, measure, baselines, frozen threshold, epsilon, guardrails, FDR plan, and max_cycles, hashed so the whole pre-commitment is auditable and tamper-evident.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any pre-committed element is amended or the record is re-hashed

pros.claim: A single hashed preregistration artifact makes the entire pre-commitment falsifiable and tamper-evident
pros.example: the record's hash is published before cycle 1, so any later edit is detectable

cons.claim: Bundling everything into one record makes legitimate mid-course amendment heavy and visible by design
cons.example: fixing one wrong guardrail bound requires re-hashing and logging an amendment to the whole record

failure_modes: the record is editable in place, so pre-registration cannot be verified
the artifact omits the stopping rule, leaving termination unpinned
acceptance_tests: the artifact is content-hashed, timestamped, and includes construct, measure, baseline, threshold, epsilon, guardrails, FDR plan and max_cycles
every amendment is appended to an immutable log rather than overwriting the artifact
revisit_triggers: an amendment is requested
the artifact is found to omit a pre-committed element

nodes.definition: Record metric provenance: for every frozen choice (construct naming, indicator, estimator, baseline, threshold, epsilon, max_cycles), capture who chose it, on what evidence, and the alternatives rejected, so the freeze is explainable and a future amendment is principled rather than ad hoc.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the provenance schema or evidence-capture policy changes

pros.claim: Provenance turns the frozen metric from an opaque constant into an explainable, amendable decision record
pros.example: 'why epsilon=0.5sigma?' is answered by the recorded power analysis and the rejected 0.2sigma option

cons.claim: Full provenance capture adds documentation overhead that teams under time pressure may skip
cons.example: logging the rationale and rejected alternatives for every choice doubles the freeze effort

failure_modes: a frozen choice has no recorded rationale, so amendments are guesses
provenance is written after the fact to justify the chosen number
acceptance_tests: each frozen choice carries an owner, the evidence used, and at least one rejected alternative
revisit_triggers: a choice must be amended without recorded rationale
the evidence behind a choice is invalidated

nodes.definition: Render the decision gate: at each cycle boundary, apply the frozen rules (improvement criterion, guardrails, FDR, stopping rule) to render an explicit stop / continue / amend decision with its justification, so loop control is a logged judgement, not drift.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the decision logic or any rule it composes changes

pros.claim: A logged decision gate makes every cycle's stop/continue/amend a justified, auditable call against the frozen rules
pros.example: cycle 5 logs 'continue: delta>=epsilon, all guardrails green, FDR-adjusted win, budget remaining'

cons.claim: A rigid gate can force a mechanically correct but contextually wrong stop, with no room for judgement
cons.example: the gate halts at max_cycles despite an obvious near-win, because the rule admits no override

failure_modes: the gate is bypassed and the loop continues on intuition
an amend verdict is used to quietly relax the frozen threshold
acceptance_tests: every cycle boundary produces a logged stop/continue/amend verdict justified by the frozen rules
revisit_triggers: a decision is overridden manually
a frozen rule the gate composes is amended

nodes.definition: Issue a termination certificate: when the loop stops, emit a record stating which arm fired (threshold crossed or max_cycles exhausted), the final metric vs baseline vs threshold, guardrail status, and FDR-adjusted significance, certifying the eval loop terminated under the frozen rules (closing R2 non-termination).

included: final metric vs baseline vs threshold
guardrail and FDR status at stop

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the certification format or the termination criteria change

pros.claim: A termination certificate makes 'the loop is done and it terminated legitimately' an inspectable artifact, closing R2
pros.example: the certificate reads 'stopped at cycle 6: M=0.052>=0.05 threshold, guardrails green, BH-significant'

cons.claim: A certificate can lend false closure if the underlying frozen rules were themselves mis-specified
cons.example: a clean certificate on a Goodharted metric certifies a hollow win

failure_modes: the loop stops with no record of which arm fired or the final comparison
a max_cycles stop is reported as a threshold success
acceptance_tests: the certificate states the firing arm, final metric/baseline/threshold, guardrail status and FDR-adjusted significance
a threshold stop and a max_cycles stop are distinguishable in the certificate
revisit_triggers: the certified result is challenged
the termination criteria are revised for the next loop

edges.why_related: detected gaming feeds back to revise or add indicators so the metric re-tracks the construct
a detected drift forces a logged amendment to the frozen metric rather than a silent edit
a guardrail breach can force a stop even before the threshold or fuel budget conditions fire
remaining fuel constrains whether the gate can return continue
estimated proxy validity sets the weight each proxy earns in the OEC
a decision-flip under sensitivity analysis routes back to the gate to withhold a stop verdict
provenance records the rationale behind each frozen choice for principled amendment
the construct-validity audit is the held-out reference Goodhart checks the metric against
per-cycle improvement pressure pushes to keep iterating while the stopping rule must eventually halt the loop
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the metric or the loop
edges.resolution_rule: the loop continues only while delta_M>=epsilon AND fuel remains AND threshold unmet; when these conflict, the stopping rule's max_cycles arm dominates to guarantee termination

edges.why_related: optimizing the OEC can push a guardrail metric past its acceptable bound
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the metric or the loop
edges.resolution_rule: accept an OEC gain only if every guardrail stays within its pre-set non-regression bound; otherwise the guardrail veto overrides the OEC improvement

edges.why_related: raw metric improvement can be Goodhart gaming rather than real construct gain
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the metric or the loop
edges.resolution_rule: a metric gain that the construct-validity audit shows is decoupled from the construct does not count as improvement, even if delta_M>=epsilon

edges.why_related: an unadjusted per-comparison improvement can be a false discovery from testing many slices
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades the metric or the loop
edges.resolution_rule: a per-niche delta counts as a win only after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment across the declared family, not on its unadjusted value

conflict_axes.name: frozen_metric_vs_adaptive_redefinition
conflict_axes.description: Freezing the metric prevents gaming the target post-hoc but blocks fixing a genuinely mis-specified metric without costly change-control.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: amend only via a logged, hashed change-control step, never a silent edit

conflict_axes.name: keep_iterating_vs_terminate
conflict_axes.description: Per-cycle improvement pressure wants to keep optimizing while the stopping rule must halt to avoid R2 non-termination.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stop at threshold OR max_cycles, whichever fires first

conflict_axes.name: metric_optimization_vs_construct_fidelity
conflict_axes.description: Pushing the metric harder raises Goodhart risk that the number rises while the construct it indexes falls.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run a held-out construct audit and discount gains that decouple from it

conflict_axes.name: single_OEC_vs_multi_metric_transparency
conflict_axes.description: One OEC makes the loop decidable but hides trade-offs that separate metrics would expose.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: optimize one OEC but bound the hidden trade-offs with guardrail metrics

conflict_axes.name: statistical_power_vs_false_discovery_control
conflict_axes.description: FDR control across many niches bounds false wins but lowers power to detect real small effects.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set the target FDR level before testing and accept the power trade-off

conflict_axes.name: epsilon_too_high_vs_too_low
conflict_axes.description: A large epsilon discards real small gains; a small epsilon lets noise read as improvement.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set epsilon just above the metric's estimated standard error

conflict_axes.name: tight_fuel_budget_vs_near_win
conflict_axes.description: A tight max_cycles guarantees a hard halt but can stop a loop one cycle short of crossing the threshold.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fix max_cycles in the frozen record; a near-win at budget end is a documented non-result, not an override

conflict_axes.name: convenient_proxy_vs_validated_proxy
conflict_axes.description: A cheap available indicator speeds the loop but a validated proxy better tracks real value.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the convenient proxy but weight it by its estimated true-value correlation

conflict_axes.name: preregistration_rigor_vs_speed
conflict_axes.description: Full construct-validation and provenance capture before iterating is rigorous but slows a fast content pipeline.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: freeze the minimum decidable bundle first; deepen validity evidence in parallel

edge_cases.description: The optimization loop has only a threshold stop and never reaches it, so it iterates forever (R2 non-termination).
edge_cases.trigger: no max_cycles fuel budget is registered alongside the threshold
edge_cases.mitigation: register max_cycles in the frozen record so the loop halts at threshold OR budget exhaustion

edge_cases.description: Disappointing results trigger a quiet redefinition of the 'frozen' metric to relabel a miss as a win (HARKing / outcome switching).
edge_cases.trigger: the metric record is editable in place with no amendment log
edge_cases.mitigation: store the metric in an immutable hashed record; any change is a dated, logged amendment

edge_cases.description: The metric keeps rising while the underlying construct degrades: pure Goodhart capture.
edge_cases.trigger: the metric is optimized with no held-out construct audit
edge_cases.mitigation: run a held-out construct check; divergence between metric and audit triggers review

edge_cases.description: Scanning many niches finds a 'win' that is just noise surfaced by multiplicity (garden of forking paths).
edge_cases.trigger: per-niche p-values are read with no FDR adjustment and the family is defined after seeing winners
edge_cases.mitigation: declare the comparison family up front and apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control

edge_cases.description: Epsilon is set below the metric's noise, so the loop 'improves' on random fluctuations.
edge_cases.trigger: epsilon chosen without reference to the metric's standard error
edge_cases.mitigation: set epsilon above the estimated standard error and verify with sensitivity analysis

edge_cases.description: A logging or pipeline change silently shifts the frozen metric, and the shift is read as a real movement.
edge_cases.trigger: the data feeding the frozen metric changes without drift detection
edge_cases.mitigation: monitor input distribution and computation hash; a change raises a drift flag, not a metric verdict

edge_cases.description: Optimizing the OEC quietly harms a metric nobody set as a guardrail (e.g. unsubscribe-rate).
edge_cases.trigger: no guardrail metric covers the harmed dimension
edge_cases.mitigation: enumerate guardrail metrics with non-regression bounds checked every cycle

edge_cases.description: The baseline is recomputed each cycle, so the anchor moves and noise is mistaken for improvement.
edge_cases.trigger: baseline is not frozen alongside the metric
edge_cases.mitigation: freeze naive and human baselines on the same population and never recompute per cycle

edge_cases.description: The max_cycles budget is silently extended because results 'look promising', defeating the termination guarantee.
edge_cases.trigger: the fuel ledger is advisory rather than enforced
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce a monotone non-renewable counter fixed in the frozen record

edge_cases.description: A win declared on one window vanishes under a slightly different reasonable specification.
edge_cases.trigger: the decision rests on a single arbitrary specification never stress-tested
edge_cases.mitigation: require the stop/continue decision to hold across a pre-declared set of reasonable specifications

edge_cases.description: Two stakeholders optimize the same metric name while privately holding different constructs.
edge_cases.trigger: the construct was never named and validated before indicators were chosen
edge_cases.mitigation: name and validate the construct with an explicit not-this list before selecting indicators

edge_cases.description: A max_cycles stop is reported as if the threshold had been crossed, hiding a non-result.
edge_cases.trigger: the termination certificate does not distinguish which stop arm fired
edge_cases.mitigation: the certificate must state the firing arm and the final metric vs threshold vs baseline

workflow.description: Turn 'the results are good' into a single named construct with a one-line definition and an explicit not-this list.
workflow.gate: construct named and agreed by >=2 stakeholders

workflow.description: Choose observable indicators with a reflective/formative stance and an indicator-to-construct hypothesis each.
workflow.gate: each indicator has a stated link to the construct

workflow.description: Estimate how well each indicator tracks real downstream value and document breakdown conditions.
workflow.gate: proxy-to-true-value correlation estimated with an interval

workflow.description: Pin the exact estimator, population, unit and window so M is reproducible.
workflow.gate: two implementations agree on the same data

workflow.description: Combine the proxies into one overall evaluation criterion with fixed weights and directions.
workflow.gate: OEC is a single function with pre-agreed weights

workflow.description: Compute a naive/random and a human-curated baseline on the same population as the live metric.
workflow.gate: both baselines computed on the comparison population

workflow.description: Lock measure, baseline and threshold into an immutable timestamped record before any optimization.
Set epsilon above the metric's standard error as the minimum per-cycle delta over the frozen baseline.
workflow.gate: epsilon exceeds the estimated standard error and is fixed

workflow.description: Define guardrail metrics with non-regression bounds and declare the FDR-controlled comparison family.
workflow.gate: guardrails bounded and comparison family declared up front

workflow.description: Register the stop-at-threshold-OR-max_cycles rule and the enforced fuel budget so termination is bounded.
workflow.gate: stop fires at threshold or max_cycles, whichever first

workflow.description: At each cycle boundary apply the frozen rules to render a logged stop/continue/amend verdict.
workflow.gate: every cycle ends with a justified verdict against the frozen rules

workflow.description: On stop, emit a certificate stating which arm fired, final metric vs baseline vs threshold, guardrail and FDR status.
workflow.gate: firing arm and final comparison recorded; R2 closed

priority_rationale: SUCCESS_CONSTRUCT/CONSTRUCT_VALIDITY/INDICATOR_SELECTION are foundational; MEASURE/OEC/BASELINE feed the freeze; FROZEN_METRIC plus IMPROVEMENT_CRITERION plus STOPPING_RULE plus FUEL_BUDGET are the termination core that closes R2; guardrails, drift, sensitivity and the decision gate gate correctness; the termination certificate closes the loop.

dominance_rules.rule: The metric, baseline and threshold must be frozen in an immutable record before the first optimization cycle
dominance_rules.rationale: an editable target lets results redraw the goal post-hoc (HARKing)
dominance_rules.trigger: optimization begins without an immutable frozen record
dominance_rules.action: block iteration until the metric+baseline+threshold are immutably registered

dominance_rules.rule: Every optimization loop must register a max_cycles fuel budget alongside its threshold
dominance_rules.rationale: a threshold-only loop can iterate forever if the threshold is never reached (R2 non-termination)
dominance_rules.trigger: a loop is configured with a threshold but no max_cycles
dominance_rules.action: require a max_cycles budget so the stopping rule halts at threshold OR budget exhaustion

dominance_rules.rule: An OEC gain must not be accepted if it breaches any guardrail's non-regression bound
dominance_rules.rationale: winning on the primary metric by harming a guardrail is a net loss
dominance_rules.trigger: a candidate improves the OEC while a guardrail regresses past its bound
dominance_rules.action: reject the candidate and route to guardrail review

dominance_rules.rule: A per-niche win must clear Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment before it is declared
dominance_rules.rationale: unadjusted multiplicity manufactures false wins across many slices
dominance_rules.trigger: a slice is declared a win on an unadjusted p-value
dominance_rules.action: apply FDR control over the declared family before declaring any win

dominance_rules.rule: Epsilon must exceed the metric's estimated standard error before iteration starts
dominance_rules.rationale: an epsilon below the noise floor declares random walk steps as improvement
dominance_rules.trigger: epsilon is set without a noise estimate
dominance_rules.action: block freeze until epsilon is shown to exceed the standard error

dominance_rules.rule: A metric gain that diverges from the held-out construct audit must not count as improvement
dominance_rules.rationale: Goodhart gaming inflates the metric while the construct falls
dominance_rules.trigger: the metric rises while the construct audit drops
dominance_rules.action: discount the gain and trigger a Goodhart review

dominance_rules.rule: Any change to a frozen element must be a logged, hashed amendment, never a silent edit
dominance_rules.rationale: silent edits make the pre-registration claim unfalsifiable
dominance_rules.trigger: a frozen value is changed in place
dominance_rules.action: reject the edit and require an appended amendment with rationale

dominance_rules.rule: The termination certificate must distinguish a threshold stop from a max_cycles stop
dominance_rules.rationale: a budget-exhaustion stop reported as a threshold success hides a non-result
dominance_rules.trigger: a certificate omits which stop arm fired
dominance_rules.action: require the firing arm and final metric/baseline/threshold in the certificate

dominance_rules.rule: The construct must be named and validated before indicators are selected
dominance_rules.rationale: choosing indicators first lets convenience define success and hides stakeholder disagreement
dominance_rules.trigger: indicators are proposed before a named, validated construct exists
dominance_rules.action: block indicator selection until the construct is named with a not-this list

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not start optimization before the metric is frozen; redefining it mid-loop invalidates every prior cycle's comparison
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running all cycles after a late metric redefinition

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run a loop without a max_cycles budget; retrofitting a stopping rule onto a runaway loop wastes the spent fuel
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency halt and re-design after a non-terminating loop burns the compute budget

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not recompute the baseline each cycle; a moving anchor forces re-deriving every prior delta
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-evaluating all historical improvements against a shifting baseline

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not set epsilon below the metric's noise; discovering the loop optimized noise forces discarding the run
anti_rework_rules.prevents: throwing away cycles that 'improved' only random fluctuations

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not read per-niche wins without FDR control; un-adjusting later means re-testing the whole family
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-litigating every slice result after a false-discovery scandal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not omit guardrails and add them post-hoc; a late guardrail breach forces re-running optimization
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-optimizing after discovering collateral harm no guardrail caught

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not edit a frozen element in place; reconstructing the original for audit requires re-deriving the history
anti_rework_rules.prevents: forensic reconstruction of a metric's true frozen value

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not select indicators before naming the construct; a late construct change invalidates the indicator-to-construct links
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-selecting and re-validating indicators after the construct is renamed

iteration_protocol.trigger: the optimization loop fails to terminate or has no registered max_cycles
iteration_protocol.action: register a max_cycles fuel budget in FUEL_BUDGET and wire it into STOPPING_RULE so the loop halts at threshold OR budget

iteration_protocol.trigger: the frozen metric is proposed for redefinition after seeing results
iteration_protocol.action: route the change through a logged, hashed amendment in PREREGISTRATION_RECORD instead of a silent edit to FROZEN_METRIC

iteration_protocol.trigger: the metric and the held-out construct audit diverge
iteration_protocol.action: trigger a Goodhart review in GOODHART and re-check PROXY_VALIDITY before counting further gains

iteration_protocol.trigger: wins are being declared across many niches without multiplicity control
iteration_protocol.action: declare the comparison family and apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control in MULTIPLE_COMPARISONS at the DECISION_GATE

iteration_protocol.trigger: a guardrail metric breaches its non-regression bound
iteration_protocol.action: reject the OEC gain in GUARDRAIL_METRICS and re-render the cycle verdict at DECISION_GATE

iteration_protocol.trigger: a drift in the frozen metric's inputs is detected
iteration_protocol.action: raise a drift flag in METRIC_DRIFT_AUDIT and hold the comparison to the frozen baseline until resolved

iteration_protocol.trigger: the stop/continue decision flips under a reasonable alternative specification
iteration_protocol.action: run SENSITIVITY_ANALYSIS and withhold the stop verdict at DECISION_GATE until the decision is robust

iteration_protocol.trigger: the loop stops without a clear record of which arm fired
iteration_protocol.action: emit a TERMINATION_CERTIFICATE distinguishing a threshold stop from a max_cycles stop with the final comparison
